title: An encoder ends a cycle at the first repeat, by identity, and never by exhausting a depth cap
scope:
what every encoder that walks a program's own value graph does when it reaches a value it
is already inside. It does not decide what the *record* renderings answer — [0092](0092.md) settled
that and this record leaves it exactly as it stands — and it does not move any depth cap, which
stays as the bound on structure that is legal but deep.
dependsOnText:
[0023](0023.md), [0006](0006.md) and [0024](0024.md), whose graph copy is the walk
that already holds this property for the two carriers it owns; [0092](0092.md), whose record model
resolves a repeat to an identity so a diagnostic rendering can link or reference it.
validatedBy:
the conformance cases the rule below names, landed by the goal that carries it.
Nothing holds this record on its own today, which is why the rule it creates is `designed`.

summary.headline: Encoding a self-containing value fails at the first repeat, naming the path
summary.body:
`Core\Json::encode` and its peers remember which objects they are currently inside, and the
first object met a second time on the way down ends the encoding with an error naming the
property chain that closed the loop, such as `user.team.owner`. A value that merely appears
twice, in two places, is written twice. The encoder never invents a marker in the document to
stand for the repeat, because the document is somebody else's contract. A separate depth limit
still exists, but it is no longer how a cycle is detected.
